newsitem.title: USA: SyQuest in talks on Rocket products.
newsitem.headline: SyQuest in talks on Rocket products.

text.p: SyQuest Technology Inc is talking with computer makers about marketing products using its new 4.7 gigabyte Rocket technology, senior company officials said on Friday.

The executives, speaking at a Robertson Stephens technology conference in San Francisco, declined to say when SyQuest would ship a product based on Rocket, though the company has demonstrated devices using the removable disk drive technology since November.

They also stressed that the company was in the middle of a "very challenging" transition and repeated warnings of lower revenues and heavier losses in its March quarter than in the first fiscal quarter to the end of December.
"Turning the business around has been and remains very challenging," SyQuest Chief Executive Ed Harper told investors in a presentation at the conference.

On a positive note, Harper said SyQuest was not shipping the SyJet product "in volume to meet demand." Order backlogs for the product were at a record high and more than double the backlog of any earlier SyQuest product, he said.
After the presentation, SyQuest shares were up as much as 1/2 to 3-5/8 before receding in midafternoon trading to 2-3/4, down 3/8.

Afterwards, SyQuest chairman Edward Marinaro told reporters the company expected to ship internal IDE versions of its EZFlyer 230 megabyte and 1.5 megabyte SyJet drives by the end of the June quarter. He also said the company had received "strong interest" from computer makers about incorporating the drives in their products.

"This is a very difficult transition quarter for us," he said. The company said it had converted $11.6 million of debt into equity. Marinaro said the company had more than $14 million in cash at the end of December and had access to cash through its banks.
Marinaro said sales in the company's legacy pre-press businesses were showing further declines, but SyQuest was addressing the situation with its new products.
"That's one of the things that is causing us substantial angst," he said, referring to the decline.
Regarding the Rocket technology, Marinaro said: "We have it as a product" but have chosen not to market it until after certain computer makers provided feedback.
Harper said the company was working to create greater manufacturing efficiencies.
"SyQuest created our marketplace but we lost our way when the Iomega folks came along," he said.
He noted the EZFlyer ran at twice the speed and had twice the capacity of the Iomega Zip drive and SyQuest's SyJet had greater capacity than the Iomega Jaz drive.
Harper also said the SyQuest removable hard drives were more durable that the Zip drive's floppy media.
He said the market for removable hard drives was expected to grow at 47 percent a year, according to Disk Trends and Dataquest data.
"Turnaround are always easier to complete in a rapidly growing market," he said.
